text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Tuesday:

-- Zurich, Switzerland's biggest city, licensed U.S. telecommunications group American Worldcom and British rival Colt Telecom to build and operate fibre optic telcoms networks on public grounds. The Swiss telecommunictaions market is due to be liberalised as of January 1, 1998, in line with the surrounding European Union.

-- Switzerland and ther United States want to open talks on an agreement for the mutual recognition of product control. U.S. ambassador Madeleine Kunin and the head of the Swiss Federal Office of Foreign Economy, Franz Blankart, reached an initial agreement on Monday. First talks are planned for September in Washington.

-- Two accounts at Zurich Kantonalbank may have belonged to prominent Nazis Willi Bauer and Elisabeth Eder. According to the Simon Wiesenthal Center in Los Angeles, Willi Bauer was the assumed name of Anton Burger, the deputy commander of Theresienstadt concentration camp. Eder was the wife of Ernst Kaltenbrunner, chief of the securitiy services in the Third Reich. A detailed inquiry by the bank is not yet complete.

-- Pharma and life sciences group Novartis, which in Switzerland says it supports separate labelling for genetically altered foodstuffs, also signed a U.S. industry letter opposing separte labelling. Novartis is a member of industry groups that wrote to U.S. President Bill Clinton a month ago opposing European Union proposals for consumer marking that clearly distinguishes gene-altered from non-altered food.

-- Old documents rescued from shredding at Switzerland's biggest bank by security guard Christoph Meili did not contain any information about dormant accounts, Union Bank of Switzerland said. But the documents may include information on property seized from Jews in Germany.

-- Police arrested about 180 people for using illegal drugs at the Paleo Festival in Nyon, one of Switzerland's leading summer music fests which finished on Sunday. Last year 220 drug users were arrested on the open-air festival.
